title: Architecture P1: defuse the MULTI_TENANCY registry upsert — it silently collapses registrations per (hash, tenant) if the flag is ever enabled
description:
**Ask:** In the same phase that touches registration (plan-sheet requirement — not later, not beside), defuse `platform_document_registry`'s armed landmine: UNIQUE `uq_pdr_hash_tenant (content_hash, tenant_id)` + `ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE` in `registerInPlatformRegistry`. Either re-key the registry on the document UUID, or explicitly remove/disable the upsert.

**Why it matters:** the code path is dormant ONLY because `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED !== 'true'` on local and demo (0 registry rows in both DBs). If that flag is ever switched on with today's code, the upsert wakes and silently collapses registration pointers — newest write wins per (hash, tenant) — which directly violates ruling (b): duplicate bytes = two registrations, distinguished by UUID. A landmine that has been found and left armed is worse than one nobody found.

**Spec:** `1_Project_Definition/architecture/2026-08-07_K-side-plan-sheet.md` ("The MULTI_TENANCY landmine — inside P1, not beside it").

nodes.body:
## Confirmed live on `develop` `541acae81` — the landmine is still armed, both halves

**The upsert**, `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:396` (read from `origin/develop`, not the working tree):

```sql
ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE SET
  document_id = EXCLUDED.document_id, title = EXCLUDED.title, status = EXCLUDED.status, updated_at = NOW()
```

**The constraint**, from the live database:

```
uq_pdr_hash_tenant   (plus platform_document_registry_pkey, idx_pdr_hash, idx_pdr_doc)
```

So both halves are present and they compose exactly as the description says: two documents with the same `content_hash` in one tenant do not collide loudly — the second **overwrites the first's `document_id`** in the registry, and the first registration stops being findable by hash. Silent, and it looks like a successful registration to the caller.

One method note, because it nearly gave me a wrong answer: my first search matched `services/originate/dist/routes/verification.d.ts` — **build output**, which is not the authority and which does not exist at `origin/develop` at all (`git show` refused it). Reading a `dist/` file would have been reading yesterday's compile. The line above is from the `src/` file at the SHA. Also: the search only ran at all once `--include=*.ts` was quoted — unquoted, zsh's `nomatch` kills grep before it starts and the result reads as a clean zero.

Sequencing point from the description stands: this belongs in the same phase as [KS-597](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-597), not after it — registration is the write path that arms it.

No code written. Left in Todo.
